decisive_items: Immunofluorescence: Large amount of IgA deposition in mesangial area
Electron Microscopy: Electron-dense deposits in mesangial area
response.rationale: Kidney biopsy shows dominant IgA mesangial deposition with crescents, diagnostic of IgA nephropathy. Serologic SLE markers are present but biopsy pattern is not typical for lupus nephritis; RPGN is a syndrome, not the underlying disease.

rejected.why: Positive ANA/anti-SM/low complement suggest SLE, but biopsy shows IgA-dominant mesangial deposits, not the typical immune-complex pattern of lupus nephritis.
Same as R3; SLE with renal involvement is less specific than biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy.
RPGN describes the clinical-pathologic syndrome (crescents, oliguria) but does not identify the underlying IgA nephropathy.
Duplicate of R5; RPGN is a syndrome, not the most specific diagnosis given IgA deposition.
